newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Kaucuk, Chemopetrol shares to halt trade Fri.
newsitem.headline: Czech Kaucuk, Chemopetrol shares to halt trade Fri.

text.p: Trading in shares of the Czech petrochemical companies Kaucuk a.s. and Chemopetrol a.s. will end after Friday's session on the Prague Stock Exchange, ahead of the completion of the merger of the companies, the PSE said on Wednesday.
"The reason for the end of trading is the elimination of these companies without liquidation," PSE spokesman Milan Vodicka said in a statement.
The petrochemical assets of the two former state companies are being merged into the joint-stock company Unipetrol a.s. which will be soon listed on the PSE, Vodicka said.
The refinery assets were hived off in 1995 and merged to form Ceska Rafinerska a.s., a subsidiary of the new Unipetrol in which a western consortium of oil companies holds a 49 percent stake.

According to agreements by the companies' shareholders earlier this year, new shares of Unipetrol are to be issued at a 12-to-1 ratio for Kaucuk stock, while shares for Chemopetrol stock will be exchanged at an 11-to-1 ratio.
Vodicka added that an administrative court had approved the creation and registration of the merger on Monday.
He told Reuters that Unipetrol can now apply for a listing on the PSE, and shares of the new company can start trading as soon as August 8 if the application is made soon.

It was not yet known whether Unipetrol will apply to be quoted on the PSE main market or the parallel market where listing requirements are less strict. Officials of Unipetrol were not immediately available for comment.
